# Aurora Aims History

How the aims of the [[aurora-programme-grant-2027]] changed between June and October 2026, and why. Use this to answer "why two aims?" or "where did the proteomics aim go?".

## Summary

> [!abstract]
> Three aims at the June kickoff, still three in the September draft sent to the mock panel, two since 2026-10-12. Proteomics moved from its own aim across both cohorts to work package 2.3 on St Aldric post-surgery plasma only.

## Versions

| Version | Date | Aims | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v1 | 2026-06-30 | 1 Pre-diagnostic timing (Northvale); 2 Post-surgery MRD (St Aldric); 3 Plasma proteomics across both | [[aurora-aims-v1]] (archived) |
| v2 | 2026-09-08 | Same three; aim 3 renamed "multi-analyte integration" | [[aurora-aims-draft-v2]] |
| v3 | 2026-10-12 | 1 Pre-diagnostic timing; 2 Relapse detection with cfDNA and proteins (WP 2.1 fragmentomics, 2.2 methylation, 2.3 proteomics) | [[aurora-aims-draft-v3]] |

## What Drove Each Change

- v1 to v2: renaming aim 3 was an attempt to answer Marta's own worry that it lacked a hypothesis. It did not change the substance.
- v2 to v3: the [[aurora-mock-panel-2026-09-29]] found aim 3 dependent on the other two and in conflict with them for Northvale plasma. See [[dependent-aims-risk]] and the answered [[should-proteomics-be-an-aurora-work-package]].
- Aim 1 wording also changed in v3: the exclusion of cases diagnosed within a year of blood draw is now stated on the aims page, at Leah Ostrander's request, consistent with the reverse-causation decision in the [[lead-time-analysis]].

## What Stayed the Same

The programme's through-line, one cfDNA feature set followed from years before diagnosis to relapse after surgery, built on the [[northvale-early-detection-study]] and the [[pancreatic-cfdna-mrd-study]].
